topic: News breakdown: Google's privacy policy now lets Gmail and Photos data you connect to its AI shape your ads
post:
Connected Gmail or Google Photos to Google's AI? Your ads may be listening. 📬
Here's what changed in Google's privacy policy, and what it means.

What happened 👇
📄 Google updated its privacy policy, effective October 16
🔓 It kept its promise not to personalize ads from your Gmail, Drive or Photos content, but added an exception: unless you choose to make that data available to other Google services that support personalized ads
🤖 That mainly covers Personal Intelligence, the opt-in feature that lets Gemini and AI Mode in Search use context from apps like Gmail and Photos

Google's side:
It says you won't see ads based directly on your inbox or photo library, it won't use sensitive information like health or religion for ads, and it won't pass personal details to advertisers without permission.

Critics' side:
The gap between "directly" and "indirectly" is doing a lot of work.

Why it matters:
AI assistants work better with your data. That same data is worth a lot to advertisers. Expect more of these trade-offs. ⚖️

Practical takeaway:
If you've connected apps to an AI assistant, review which ones this week. Keep the ones you use, disconnect the rest. 🔍

Would you trade some privacy for a smarter assistant? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
